description: The input half of Stage 1, in a new file native/ios/TouchControls.swift: the wire format of engine.applyGamepad stated once and derived nowhere else, the per-system control sets, an editor-ready layout value, and a multi-touch UIView that treats the D-pad as one surface. This is the point of Stage 1: the engine exposes apply_gamepad(port:buttons:axes:) and connectedPads() through UniFFI and nothing in Swift has ever called either, so no game can be started, paused or played.
steps: Establish the wire format BEFORE writing any control code, by reading the engine rather than assuming libretro's order. Trace: uniffi_api.rs:548 apply_gamepad -> bridge.rs:554 apply_gamepad -> input/gamepad.rs apply_standard_gamepad, which indexes the incoming array through STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP (gamepad.rs:106-123), the W3C standard gamepad layout. Encode that as a `PadSlot` enum whose rawValue IS the array index, with a doc comment naming the three files the contract passes through, and build every array through it so no call site can ever write a bare integer.

Define `PadFrame`, the value pushed to the engine: exactly 16 booleans and exactly 4 floats, built from a set of PadSlot. Assert the lengths in the type itself (fixed-size construction, not an append loop) so a short or long array cannot be produced. Comment that missing entries would be tolerated by `buttons.get(index)` on the Rust side but that sending exactly 16 and 4 is what makes the contract legible.

Define `GameSystem`: nes, snes, gb, gbc, gba, sms, gg, genesis, ps1. Each carries a short badge string, a display name, and its control set. This is the dimension CoreCatalog's routing table was missing: coreId alone cannot drive the layout, because mgba is gba plus gb plus gbc and genesis_plus_gx is genesis plus sms plus gg, and those need different button counts.

Define the per-system control sets, with every face button mapping taken from the upstream core source read during planning and cited in a comment, never from the button's name. NES and GB and GBC: D-pad, B, A, SELECT, START. GBA: the same plus L and R. SNES: D-pad, B, A, Y, X, L, R, SELECT, START. Mega Drive: D-pad, A, B, C, START, where A is retro Y, B is retro B and C is retro A per Genesis-Plus-GX libretro/libretro.c (descriptors at ~2958, DEVICE_PAD3B falling through to DEVICE_PAD2B at ~479). Master System and Game Gear: D-pad, 1, 2, START, where 1 is retro B and 2 is retro A from the same two-button path. PS1: D-pad, Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, L1, R1, L2, R2, SELECT, START, per pcsx_rearmed frontend/libretro.c:1965-1968 (retro B, A, X, Y respectively). No analog sticks in Stage 1: the axes are sent as four zeroes, which is correct rather than a stub, because apply_standard_gamepad ORs the stick-derived D-pad onto the button bits and therefore cannot cancel a button-driven direction.

Define `TouchLayout` as the SAME six numbers the browser build used (web/src/data/touch-layout.js): scale, opacity, dpadX, dpadY, faceX, faceY, with the same LIMITS and the same clamping on read. Stage 1 ships NO editor UI and only ever uses `TouchLayout.standard`, but taking the layout as a parameter now is what makes the user-editable layout in FEAT-006 an addition rather than a rewrite of the layout engine.

Write `TouchControlsView: UIView` with isMultipleTouchEnabled = true. Multi-touch is not optional: holding a direction while pressing a face button is most of playing a game, and a single-touch implementation would leave the app as unplayable as it is now in a way that looks like a subtle bug. Track `[ObjectIdentifier: Grab]` keyed on UITouch identity, because a UITouch object is the same instance across began, moved, ended and cancelled and is the only reliable way to know which finger let go of what.

Make the grab sticky for chips and live for the D-pad. `case chip(Int)` keeps its control until the finger lifts, which mirrors the browser's setPointerCapture and stops thumb drift releasing a held button mid-jump. `case dpad(CGPoint)` stores the touch point and is recomputed on every move, which is what makes sliding from Up to Up-Right work.

Recompute the whole pressed state from the grab dictionary on every touch event rather than incrementing and decrementing per-control counters. Two fingers on one button, a cancelled touch and a gesture-recogniser steal all then resolve correctly by construction, with no reference-count bug to have.

Port the D-pad surface maths from web/src/engine/input.js _attachDpadSurface EXACTLY, constants included: normalise the point to the pad centre over its half extents, require magnitude > 0.22, and light a direction when its component dominates, abs(y) > abs(x) * 0.42. SESSION_HANDOFF.md's appendix records the single-surface decision from the browser build as a decision to follow, so the numbers are carried across rather than re-derived. Note in a comment that UIKit's y axis points down exactly as the browser's clientY did, so y < 0 meaning Up is correct rather than inverted.

Derive every control size from the available play area instead of hardcoding points, and only then apply layout.scale, clamped so the widest row still fits. This is the actual fix for the overlap bug in docs/mobile-player.png: that layout collided because control positions and sizes were fixed while the space they sat in was not.

Lay the controls out in reserved, non-overlapping regions inside the safe area: shoulders as a row above the thumb clusters, D-pad bottom-left, face cluster bottom-right, SELECT and START in the bottom centre between them. Clamp every computed rect into the play area as a final pass so nothing can leave the screen in either orientation.

Then verify the layout at runtime rather than trusting the maths: after laying out, test every pair of control rects for intersection and report any overlap through a diagnostic callback naming both controls. A wrong letterbox is easy to miss and a wrong control layout is exactly the bug the reference screenshot captured, so it gets a live assertion instead of a code comment.
Override point(inside:with:) to return true ONLY inside a control rect, so taps on the picture and on the chrome above pass straight through and the controls view cannot swallow the back button.

Release everything on didMoveToWindow when leaving the window, and expose releaseAll() for the player screen to call when it leaves or the app backgrounds, so a finger down when the view disappears cannot leave a button held forever.

Wrap it for SwiftUI as `TouchControlsHost: UIViewRepresentable`, passing the system, the layout and the diagnostic callback, and handing the owner a way to read the current PadFrame synchronously from the render loop.
acceptance_criteria: The 16-entry button array is built in W3C standard gamepad order (0 B, 1 A, 2 Y, 3 X, 4 L, 5 R, 6 L2, 7 R2, 8 Select, 9 Start, 10 L3, 11 R3, 12 Up, 13 Down, 14 Left, 15 Right), matching STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP, and the axes array is 4 floats. No call site writes a raw index.
Every array sent to applyGamepad has exactly 16 booleans and exactly 4 floats, by construction rather than by convention.

The D-pad is ONE hit region whose touch position decides the directions, so a thumb between Up and Right presses both, with deadzone 0.22 and diagonal ratio 0.42 carried over from the browser implementation.
Multi-touch works: a direction held on the D-pad and a face button pressed simultaneously both reach the engine.
Lifting one finger releases only what that finger held, tracked by UITouch identity.
Each system shows only the buttons it has: 5 controls for NES, GB and GBC; 7 for GBA; 9 for SNES; 5 for Mega Drive; 4 for Master System and Game Gear; 11 for PS1.

Mega Drive A, B, C send retro Y, B, A and NOT retro A, B, C; Master System and Game Gear 1 and 2 send retro B and A; PS1 Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle send retro B, A, Y, X. Each mapping cites its upstream source in a comment.

No control rect overlaps another and none leaves the safe area, in portrait or landscape, at any layout scale the LIMITS allow; an overlap is reported through the diagnostic callback rather than shipped silently.
The layout is a parameter of the same six numbers the browser used, so FEAT-006 can add an editor without touching the layout engine.
Touches outside a control rect are not intercepted.
swiftc -frontend -parse native/ios/TouchControls.swift exits 0, and the file is listed in project.yml sources.
No em dashes anywhere in the file.
verification: swiftc -frontend -parse native/ios/TouchControls.swift -> exit 0. SPELL-CHECK ONLY, so the items below are checked by eye.
By eye against crates/emulator-bridge/src/input/gamepad.rs STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP: index by index, all 16.
By eye against crates/emulator-bridge/src/input/mod.rs: AXIS_COUNT is 4, and the Button enum is NOT the wire order, which is the trap.
By eye against web/src/engine/input.js _attachDpadSurface: the two constants and the dominance test transcribe exactly.

By eye: the grab dictionary is keyed on UITouch identity, is written in touchesBegan and touchesMoved and removed in both touchesEnded and touchesCancelled, and the pressed state is recomputed from it rather than mutated incrementally.
By eye: every control rect is derived from bounds inset by safeAreaInsets, and the unit size falls out of the available space before scale is applied.
By eye: nothing in this file touches EngineHost, so no @MainActor boundary is crossed; the file deals only in UIKit views and plain values.
grep for an em dash in the file -> no match.
Per-system control counts confirmed by reading the control set table.

STRONGER THAN -parse, and worth repeating on any change to this file: the UIKit-free half of TouchControls.swift (PadSlot, PadFrame, PadCluster, PadControlShape, PadControl, GameSystem, TouchLayout, the overlap geometry and the D-pad maths) can be EXTRACTED VERBATIM BY SCRIPT into a plain Swift file and both type-checked and RUN on Linux, because it imports nothing but Foundation. Doing that executed 70 assertions against the shipping code: array lengths and slot indices, every per-system control count, every face mapping against the upstream cores, the D-pad cardinals and diagonals plus a sweep of the whole surface for an impossible pair, the layout clamps including NaN, and the overlap geometry in both directions (that a real collision IS reported and that the diamond is NOT).

The layout arithmetic was transcribed into a simulation and run for all nine systems in portrait and landscape at scale 0.7, 1.0, 1.3 and 1.6: zero overlaps, nothing off screen, and the smallest face button 51.1 points, which clears the 44 point minimum for a touch target.
On-device behaviour (a real diagonal in Super Mario World, a held direction plus a face button, no stuck button after backgrounding) can only be verified by the orchestrator's device test.
findings: native/ios/TouchControls.swift is new and self-contained: it imports UIKit and SwiftUI only, and touches no engine type, so nothing in it can cross an actor boundary into EngineHost. THE CONTRACT, which the briefing was right to flag as the thing not to guess: applyGamepad does NOT take libretro's joypad order. Traced uniffi_api.rs:548 -> bridge.rs:554 -> gamepad.rs apply_standard_gamepad, whose STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP is the W3C standard gamepad layout, so the array is 0 B, 1 A, 2 Y, 3 X, 4 L, 5 R, 6 L2, 7 R2, 8 Select, 9 Start, 10 L3, 11 R3, 12 Up, 13 Down, 14 Left, 15 Right. libretro's own order (B 0, Y 1, Select 2, Start 3, Up 4, Down 5, Left 6, Right 7, A 8, X 9, L 10, R 11) is the Button enum in input/mod.rs and is what the core is finally asked for, but it is NOT the wire format; sending it would put Y where A belongs and Start where X belongs. That is encoded as PadSlot, whose rawValue is the index, and PadFrame builds a fixed 16-slot array plus 4 zeroed axes so a wrong length is not expressible. Two further facts from the same read shaped the design: apply_standard_gamepad REPLACES the gamepad source layer on every call, which is why the frame must be pushed every tick rather than on touch-down (FEAT-002), and the left stick ORs a synthesised D-pad onto the button bits past a 0.35 deadzone, so zeroed axes provably cannot cancel a button-driven direction. PER-SYSTEM MAPPINGS were read from the upstream sources over the network during planning rather than assumed, and that corrected one of them: Genesis-Plus-GX libretro/libretro.c (descriptors at ~2958, DEVICE_PAD3B falling through to DEVICE_PAD2B at ~479) maps retro Y to Mega Drive A, retro B to B and retro A to C, so a pad labelled A B C in alphabetical retro order would have been wrong on two of three buttons; the same two-button path gives Master System and Game Gear 1 and 2 as retro B and A. pcsx_rearmed frontend/libretro.c:1965-1968 gives Cross, Circle, Triangle, Square as retro B, A, X, Y. MULTI-TOUCH is a UIView with isMultipleTouchEnabled and a [ObjectIdentifier: Grab] map keyed on UITouch identity; the whole pressed state is recomputed from that map on every event, so two fingers on one button and a cancelled touch cannot desynchronise a counter. A chip grab is sticky until the finger lifts (mirroring the browser's pointer capture, so thumb drift cannot release a held button), while a D-pad grab stores its point and is recomputed on move, which is what makes sliding into a diagonal work. THE D-PAD is one hit region and the maths is transcribed from web/src/engine/input.js _attachDpadSurface with its constants intact (deadzone 0.22, diagonal ratio 0.42); UIKit's y axis points down like the browser's clientY, so the up test is unchanged. LAYOUT sizes the control unit from the safe-area play area and only then applies scale, clamped so the widest row still fits, which is the real fix for the overlap in docs/mobile-player.png; after layout, every pair of controls is tested for overlap and any collision is reported through onDiagnostic rather than shipped. point(inside:with:) returns true only inside a control, so the picture and the chrome above stay tappable. THE OVERLAP CHECK IS SHAPE AWARE, AND THAT IS A BUG CAUGHT BY VERIFICATION RATHER THAN BY READING. It was written first as a rectangle intersection, which is wrong: a face diamond puts four circles of diameter 1.4 units at offsets of 1.15, so the circles are hypot(1.15, 1.15) = 1.63 apart and clear each other by 0.23, while their bounding BOXES overlap at the corners because 1.15 is less than 1.4. Simulating the layout for all nine systems in both orientations reported four collisions on every pass for SNES and PS1, and because a collision report also writes the status line, it would have buried every real diagnostic behind a permanent false alarm on exactly the two systems with the most buttons. The test is now circle-to-circle, circle-to-rect (nearest point on the rect) and rect-to-rect, with half a point of slack so controls laid out edge to edge do not read as a fault. Hit testing was changed to match, for a second reason: a bounding-box test would let a thumb in the empty corner between Triangle and Circle press whichever happened to be earlier in the array, so a round control is hit-tested as a circle and a button is pressed when it looks pressed. The layout is the browser's six numbers with the browser's LIMITS, so the editor the user asked for is a later addition and not a rewrite.
